content.comment_body: Hello, I've set up communication between [product_name] and [product_name]. In my network, [product_name] acts as the server, similar to the example provided. My question is about controlling the same variable across both devices. For instance, I use a counter on [product_name] to store a value that is retrieved from [product_name] (specifically via the webserver), meaning the data flows [product_name] <- [product_name]. I also want the ability to change the value from [product_name] using a message and have it update the variable on [product_name]. As it stands, I can change the value on [product_name] or adjust the direction to only allow updates from [product_name]. How should I set up the connection to allow updates to the value from both devices and enable bi-directional data transfer? Thanks in advance for any suggestions.
Unfortunately, this isn't possible. You can either update from [product_name] or from the [product_name] display (or the [product_name] operator device), but not simultaneously from both.
Thank you for letting me know.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to set up bi-directional control and synchronization of a variable between two [company_name] devices, aiming to update and share values between both sides. However, the current system only allows updates from one device or direction at a time, preventing simultaneous dynamic modifications by both. This restricts flexibility for users wanting collaborative or distributed control using networked [product_name] hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to update the same variable from either [product_name] or [product_name], with both devices having the capability to send and receive changes to that variable.
